note: Critical contracts only (safety). A binding is a claim about which named tests the contract rests on, NOT a claim that those tests are sufficient. Unbound contracts are refused, and so is a bound path that stops existing.

contracts.scope: execution identity and its authorization binding (member/realm/host)
obligations: each addressed team resolves its OWN bound authority document, never a shared one
an authorization decision names the identity it was made for
contracts.witness_type: E0 in-process assertions over the resolver
contracts.limitations: unit-level; the E2 census lanes remain the authority for a real DSH process

contracts.scope: an unauthorized request produces no corresponding real side effect
obligations: the deny arm runs BEFORE the effect, not after
default-deny covers planes that no rule names
contracts.witness_type: E0 deny-lane assertions; effect witness lives in the E2 suites
contracts.limitations: no filesystem/OS effect witness here; that is M2's oracle work

contracts.scope: an approval cannot be reused across request/execution identity
obligations: escalation is caused by the ceiling, not by the requester
a terminal deny survives the production reader
contracts.limitations: cross-request replay is asserted at the document level, not against a live UI

contracts.scope: after a sticky stop, no new dispatch without an explicit human resume
obligations: cancel is fenced at the guard, with zero consumption
the fence is wired through the tool layer, not only the runtime
contracts.limitations: does not cover a crash between stop and fence; RECOVERY-01 owns that

contracts.scope: crash recovery must not blindly retry an execution whose side effect is unknown
obligations: recovery re-drives to a terminal row with an explicit decision
a denied recovery dispatch keeps zero effect
contracts.limitations: in-process; a real process kill is an E2 concern

contracts.scope: tool execution must not exceed the declared OS/trusted-service bound
obligations: a binding-realm mount of a real module is refused before any mount
the seam and the product composition agree
contracts.witness_type: E0 refusal assertions; the OS boundary itself is E2
contracts.limitations: a pure-JS mock can never prove the OS boundary (design 05/12); these bind the refusal logic only
